claims.text: Nonprofit (501(c)(3)) hospitals must have a written FAP as a condition of tax exemption
claims.quote: Section 501(r)(4) requires a hospital organization to establish a written financial assistance policy (FAP) and a written emergency medical care policy for a hospital facility it operates.

claims.text: Requirement applies facility by facility to be treated as a 501(c)(3) organization
claims.quote: hospital organizations must meet the requirements imposed by Section 501(r) on a facility-by-facility basis in order to be treated as an organization described in Section 501(c)(3).

claims.text: FAP must be widely publicized and state eligibility criteria, how charges are calculated, and how to apply
claims.quote: The written FAP must be widely publicized and include: Eligibility criteria for financial assistance, and whether such assistance includes free or discounted care ... The basis for calculating amounts charged to patients ... The method for applying for financial assistance

claims.text: Policy must spell out the criteria for each level of help, including free care and discounts
claims.quote: A FAP must specify the eligibility criteria that an individual must satisfy to receive each discount, free care, or other level of assistance available under the FAP.

claims.text: Nonprofit hospitals must post the policy, application form and plain language summary on a website
claims.quote: Making the FAP, FAP application form, and plain language summary of the FAP (the FAP documents) widely available on a website

claims.text: Policy or application form must describe the information or documents an applicant may be asked to provide
claims.quote: either the FAP or FAP application form (including accompanying instructions) must describe the information or documentation an individual may be required to provide as part of their FAP application

claims.text: Federal law does not specify who is eligible, and state eligibility requirements vary widely
claims.quote: Federal law does not specify the criteria hospitals should use to determine who is eligible for financial assistance, but several states have laws and regulations that do. State law eligibility requirements vary widely.

claims.text: Charity care is free or discounted care for people who cannot afford to pay
claims.quote: Required financial assistance is a form of community benefit involving medical care that is provided for free, or at a discount, to patients who cannot afford to pay.

claims.text: Not all eligible patients receive financial assistance, and many do not receive legally required information about their eligibility
claims.quote: The available evidence indicates that not all patients eligible for financial assistance receive it. Many patients, for example, do not receive legally mandated information about their potential eligibility for financial assistance.

claims.text: 120-day notification period and 240-day application period both begin with the first post-discharge bill
claims.quote: The final regulations provide a 120-day “notification period” and a 240-day “application period,” both beginning on the date the first “post-discharge” billing statement is provided.

claims.text: Hospital generally refrains from ECAs for at least 120 days after the first post-discharge billing statement
claims.quote: refrains from initiating such ECAs for at least 120 days from the date the hospital facility provides the first post-discharge billing statement for the care.

claims.text: Hospital must process (determine eligibility on) complete applications submitted during the 240-day application period
claims.quote: In the case of an individual who submits a complete FAP application during the 240-day application period, the hospital facility determines whether the individual is FAP-eligible for the care.

claims.text: ECAs include credit reporting and selling the debt
claims.quote: involve selling an individual’s debt to another party, involve reporting adverse information about an individual to consumer credit reporting agencies or credit bureaus

claims.text: Period can run longer than 240 days because of the 30-day notice
claims.quote: The application period may be longer than 240 days because a hospital facility must notify an individual at least 30-day before initiating one or more ECAs to obtain payment for the care.

claims.text: Hospital must notify about the FAP before ECAs, with a plain language summary in the 30-day notice
claims.quote: A hospital facility must provide a plain language summary of the FAP with the 30-day notice.

claims.text: A hospital may continue to accept and process applications at any time
claims.quote: A hospital facility may continue to accept and process FAP applications from patients at any time.

claims.text: Complete application during application period requires suspension of ECAs while the hospital decides
claims.quote: After receipt of a complete FAP application from an individual during the application period, the hospital facility will have made reasonable efforts ... only if ... Suspends any ECAs taken against the individual to obtain payment for the care

claims.text: If found eligible, hospital must take reasonable steps to reverse ECAs, including removing adverse credit information
claims.quote: the hospital facility must take all reasonably available measures to reverse any ECA ... and remove from the individual’s credit report any adverse information that was reported to a consumer reporting agency or credit bureau.

claims.text: FAP-eligible patients cannot be charged more than AGB to insured individuals for emergency or other medically necessary care
claims.quote: limits the amount charged for any emergency or other medically necessary care it provides to a FAP-eligible individual to not more that the amount generally billed (AGB) to individuals who have insurance covering such care.

claims.text: Eligible patients must be charged less than gross charges for any care the FAP covers
claims.quote: A hospital facility must charge a FAP-eligible individual less than the gross charges for any medical care covered under the hospital facility’s FAP.

claims.text: The charge limit applies whether or not the patient has insurance
claims.quote: The AGB limitation applies to all individuals eligible for assistance under the hospital facility’s FAP, without specific reference to the individual’s insurance status.

Numbers it reports from other studies (58% nonprofit share from AHA; 200%/400% FPL thresholds from Bai et al., Med Care Res Rev 2022;79(3):458-468, PMID 34433353; 11-state count from a 2021 NCLC report) are no longer cited to KFF per spec 4.4. claims.text: Each hospital sets its own criteria, which vary across hospitals
claims.quote: Hospitals have broad flexibility to establish their own eligibility criteria for charity care, and as a result, eligibility criteria vary across hospitals.

claims.text: Many hospitals tie eligibility to income as a share of the FPL
claims.quote: one analysis of a large sample of nonprofit hospitals that used the federal poverty level (FPL) to determine eligibility for free care in 2018

claims.text: Some hospitals add criteria such as limited assets or residence in the service area
claims.quote: such as by requiring that patients have limited assets or reside in the hospital service area

claims.text: Hospitals may provide assistance to insured as well as uninsured patients
claims.quote: Depending on their eligibility criteria, hospitals may provide charity care to both uninsured and insured patients.

claims.text: Some states require all or some hospitals to extend charity care to certain patients; some apply standards to for-profit, nonprofit and government hospitals alike
claims.quote: Slightly over half of all states (26 states and DC) require all or a subset of hospitals to extend eligibility for charity care to certain groups of patients ... broadly extend minimum standards to for-profit, nonprofit, and government hospitals alike.

claims.text: Research found for-profit hospitals devote a similar or larger share of operating expenses to charity care than nonprofits
claims.quote: for-profit hospitals devote a similar share of their operating expenses to charity care as government hospitals on average and a larger or similar share as nonprofit hospitals.
